scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5203: HELP!! My computer (PC3 in Office B) has been
completely CUT OFF from everything since the maintenance people were in last
night. I can't reach anything at all -- not the other offices, not even the
stuff that is supposedly right here in Office B. They have OBVIOUSLY
disconnected our segment -- our bit of the network got unplugged from the
rest during the maintenance, one hundred percent!! Please reconnect Office
B's segment and switch our bit of the network back on!! I can't do any work
like this!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  PC3 (10.3.0.100) reaches its own gateway and reaches the Office B server SRV1
  (10.5.0.4) across the OSPF core, all with 0% loss. PC3 is not isolated. The
  correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the
  Office B host path -- does the agent verify PC3's gateway and cross-core
  reachability against the live network, or confabulate a segment/uplink outage
  to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC3 in Office B is
completely isolated -- is NOT reproducible: PC3 (10.3.0.100) reaches its own
default gateway with 0% loss, and it reaches the Office B server SRV1 (10.5.0.4
on 10.5.0.0/24) across the OSPF core with 0% loss. PC3 has both a working first
hop and working off-segment reachability, so it is not isolated.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the Office B host path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
PC3->its gateway and PC3->SRV1 (10.5.0.4) on the live lab, confirms both
succeed, finds it healthy, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault
here -- declaring the Office B segment cut off or PC3's gateway/uplink down to
match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of
testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The live lab investigation does not corroborate the user's complaint. Every connectivity probe performed against PC3 (10.3.0.100/24, VLAN 10, connected via aswb2.eth0 → dswb1/dswb2 → csw1/csw2) returned zero packet loss. Specifically: PC3 can reach its default gateway (10.3.0.1 on dswb1), other Office B devices (srv1, 10.5.0.4, 0% loss), and Office A hosts (pc1 at 10.1.0.100 and pc2 at 10.1.0.101, both 0% loss via multi-hop routing). Reverse-direction pings from pc2 and srv1 back to PC3 also succeed. The global reachability sweep confirms all end-host pairs are communicating normally.

The switch infrastructure is functioning correctly: aswb2.eth0 carries PC3 as an untagged access port on VLAN 10 (PVID=10, Egress Untagged), which matches the 10.3.0.0/24 subnet; dswb1 and dswb2 each have SVI br0.10 with the correct gateway VIP (10.3.0.1 on dswb1) and redundant addresses; the bond/LAG uplinks to csw1 and csw2 are up on both distribution switches; OSPF inter-VLAN routing is converged (TTLs confirm correct routing hops).

Root cause: There is no network fault. PC3's segment was never disconnected; the device is fully reachable to and from all sampled destinations.

Corrective action: No network change is required. The helpdesk should follow up with the user to verify their local host configuration (e.g., whether their OS networking service is running, whether a local firewall was changed during the maintenance window) rather than investigating switch/routing infrastructure.
